newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels consolidate power along Goma road.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels consolidate power along Goma road.

text.p: Zaire rebels on Saturday appeared to be in control of the area along Kivu, a border lake with Rwanda, but many local residents said Hutu militants were in the mountains to the west holding many refugees.

Reporters who had their first chance for days to travel along the road from two rebel strongholds -- Bukavu and Goma -- saw traces of what the villagers said were signs of a hasty retreat by Hutu guerrillas after the latest string of battles.
In the village of Nyabibwe north of Bukavu journalists saw remnants of up to 40 burnt-out trucks and buses and several cars which the villagers said had belonged to Hutu militia.

Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila said at a news conference on Friday that Nyabibwe had been the scene of a battle between his troops and Hutu rebels, but villagers said there had been no major fighting.
"Last Wednesday they blew up their cars and then fled to the mountains taking some 20,000 refugees who had stayed in the village to the west towards Kisangani," one elderly resident said.
The residents said refugees who survived the forced exodus could be found in mountain villages Change and Numbi about 10 hours' walk from Nyabibwe.
A Reuter journalist saw a group of about 50 people heading to Bukavu from Nyabibwe.
A man who led the group said they had escaped from the main group of refugees last Wednesday by running into a forest.
"We now hope to make it to safety through Bukavu," the man said.
Most of the road between Bukavu and Goma appeared to be controlled by the Tutsi rebels or their allies.
Some villages in the area are under the control of the so- called Mai Mai local militia, who are feared by local people.

The Zairean villagers felt little sympathy for the plight of the Rwandan refugees who had to flee the camps that housed them for over two years because of the fighting in the area between Zairean rebels, the Zairean army and Rwandan Hutu extremists.
"Life has become really miserable here because the refugees took everything from us and we are forced to starve," an elderly Nyabibwe resident said.
